name: Fireworks AI serverless token pricing + serverless GPU hourly rates (2026-10-04 list price)
region: Fireworks cloud (US); no regional GPU SKU to price
price_basis: TWO UNITS IN ONE RECORD, DO NOT MIX THEM. (a) USD per 1M TOKENS, serverless, list price: models up to 16B parameters $0.50 input / $1.00 cached / $1.00 output / $2.00 output-cached; 16.1B-80B $3.00 / $6.00 / $6.00 / $12.00; 80B-300B (e.g. Qwen3-235B, gpt-oss-120B) $6.00 / $12.00 / $12.00 / $24.00; over 300B (e.g. DeepSeek V3, Kimi K2) $10.00 / $20.00 / $20.00 / $40.00. (b) USD per GPU-HOUR for the same company's serverless GPU product: H100 80GB $0.134/min = $8.00/hr and H200 141GB $0.134/min = $8.00/hr; B200 180GB $0.217/min = $13.00/hr; B300 288GB $0.250/min = $15.00/hr; GB300 288GB $0.334/min = $20.00/hr. price_usd = 80B-300B tier serverless input.
notes: This record deliberately carries both units because Fireworks is the one provider in this set that sells the SAME hardware two ways on one page, and the relationship between the two prices is the most useful thing a reader can learn from it. $8.00 per H100-hour divided by a 1M-token rate of, say, $12.00 for an 80-300B model implies break-even at roughly 666,667 output tokens per GPU-hour - and against the >300B rate of $40.00 it is 5,000,000 tokens per GPU-hour. Compare that with a real decode ceiling of a few thousand tok/s: a single H100 at 2,000 tok/s for a full hour produces about 7.2M output tokens, so the per-token serverless rate is genuinely competitive only for dense high-throughput serving, and the per-GPU rate wins as soon as you can keep the card busy. That crossover is the whole serverless-vs-GPU decision and it moves with your achieved tok/s, not with the list price. Note also Fireworks prices per-PARAMETER-SIZE BAND rather than per named model, so a new release inside a band is priced by the band automatically.
